sentences.text: This animal possessed thirty-nine cervical vertebrae, with neck morphology more similar to Thalassiodracon than to Plesiosaurus.
The premaxilla bears four or five alveoli and five teeth, representing a primitive feature for plesiosaurs.
The mandible retains a prominent mandibular ridge, a feature lost in other plesiosaurids.
Evidence from a subadult specimen suggests plesiosaurs retained reptilian scaly skin, unlike some other Mesozoic marine reptiles.
The only known species is represented by two immature specimens, with the subadult reaching a length of 3 meters.
The species Plesiopterys wildi was named by Frank Robin O'Keefe in 2004.
The specific name wildi honors German paleontologist Rupert Wild for his work on Mesozoic vertebrate paleobiology.
Researchers suggest the scales may have aided swimming or protected flippers during feeding on the seafloor.
Phylogenetic analyses place Plesiopterys as a sister taxon to Franconiasaurus and the clade Cryptoclidia, more derived than Microcleididae.
Plesiopterys lived during the Toarcian stage, between 184.2 and 182.9 million years ago.
It is debated whether Plesiopterys is a distinct genus or a junior synonym of Seeleyosaurus guilelmiimperatoris, with recent studies arguing for its validity.
